title: Ginsenoside Rk3 alleviates radiation nephropathy by attenuating apoptosis and inflammatory response.
authors: Wang, Mengyang; Liu, Wei; Cui, Xiaoli; Liu, Chang; Shang, Fanfan; Yang, Di
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 研究人参皂苷Rk3通过p53/MYC/STAT1通路缓解放射性肾病，仅涉及转录因子作为信号通路节点，无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiation nephropathy (RN) is a common complication of radiotherapy for abdominal or pelvic cancers, with no ideal treatment currently available. Ginsenoside Rk3, a rare ginseng saponin, possesses broad biological activities; however, its role in RN remained unclear. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of ginsenoside Rk3 against RN and to elucidate its underlying mechanism. METHOD: A renal injury model was established in C57BL/6 mice using cobalt-60 gamma-irradiation. The mice were administered ginsenoside Rk3 via daily oral gavage for 14 days. Renal histological changes were assessed using immunofluorescence staining. To identify key therapeutic targets, RNA sequencing was combined with network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses. The kidney protective mechanism mediated by ginsenoside Rk3 was clarified by measuring apoptotic levels in NRK-52E cells using flow cytometry. RESULTS: Ginsenoside Rk3 treatment ameliorated radiation-induced renal impairment and significantly reduced renal fibrosis and inflammation through the tumor protein p53 (p53) signaling pathway. It was demonstrated that ginsenoside Rk3 markedly reduced apoptosis in NRK-52E cells via this mechanism. These findings indicated that targeting the p53 signaling pathway represents a viable therapeutic strategy for preventing radiation-induced kidney injury. Furthermore, regulation of the transcription factor myelocytomatosis oncogene (MYC) and subsequent promotion of signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) expression were identified as key events downstream of p53 signaling. CONCLUSION: This study revealed that ginsenoside Rk3 effectively alleviated RN by inhibiting the p53/MYC/STAT1 and NF-kappaB signaling pathways. These findings elucidate its mechanism of action and provide new insights for future research.
abstract_zh: 背景：放射性肾病（radiation nephropathy, RN）是腹部或盆腔癌症放疗的常见并发症，目前尚无理想治疗方法。人参皂苷Rk3是一种稀有人参皂苷，具有广泛的生物活性；然而，其在RN中的作用尚不清楚。本研究旨在探讨人参皂苷Rk3对RN的保护作用，并阐明其潜在机制。方法：使用钴-60伽马射线照射在C57BL/6小鼠中建立肾损伤模型。通过每日口服灌胃给予小鼠人参皂苷Rk3，持续14天。使用免疫荧光染色评估肾组织学变化。为识别关键治疗靶点，将RNA测序与网络药理学和分子对接分析相结合。通过流式细胞术测量NRK-52E细胞中的凋亡水平，阐明人参皂苷Rk3介导的肾脏保护机制。结果：人参皂苷Rk3治疗改善了辐射诱导的肾功能损伤，并通过肿瘤蛋白p53（p53）信号通路显著减少肾纤维化和炎症。研究表明，人参皂苷Rk3通过该机制显著降低NRK-52E细胞的凋亡。这些发现表明，靶向p53信号通路是预防辐射诱导肾损伤的可行治疗策略。此外，转录因子髓细胞瘤病致癌基因（MYC）的调控及随后信号转导和转录激活因子1（STAT1）表达的促进，被确定为p53信号下游的关键事件。结论：本研究揭示，人参皂苷Rk3通过抑制p53/MYC/STAT1和NF-kappaB信号通路有效缓解RN。这些发现阐明了其作用机制，并为未来研究提供了新见解。
